q: the kosina 21 people, from a carniolan cottage where three infants died in eight years to an autumn in senj that took three grown k senj and carniola - 6 generations · 10 people from the family tree, 6 read out of the parish registers, and 5 more of the same household the kosina 21 people, from a carniolan cottage where three infants died in eight years to an autumn in senj that took three grown kosina in thirteen months - the family hedviga's own aunt married into, and for a long time the family this archive could not see. 21 people 1738 earliest birth - a kosinar woman, carniola 3 dead in 1943 this family had no page here until a week ago, and the reason was a rule rather than a doubt. this archive publishes the people of eight surnames, and kosina is not one of the eight - so ten people who are as much a part of this family as anyone in it were nowhere on the site. they existed here only in fragments: a name on a list of the senj dead, a marriage that brought the boras in, and one line cut at the foot of somebody else's gravestone. the rule changed on 21 september 2026. what decides publication now is descent and not the spelling of a surname, so everyone drawn on this page has a page of their own - apart from two who may still be living, and those two are named and nothing more. they join this family twice over. in 1919 pavao kosina married anka blazevic , the daughter of juraj blazevic and tereza zubrinic - hedviga's own grandparents . that makes anka hedviga's aunt , her father's sister, and the five kosina children of that marriage hedviga's first cousins . and pavao's own mother was angelika boras - the woman through whom the boras enter this archive at all. so two of this archive's eight families meet in one senj household , and it is this one. 16 november 1841 · kranj-smartin, book page 64 and then the slovene register was opened, and there he was the 1888 marriage named the parish. this archive stopped at the border, because croatian registers do. they did not have to: the nadskofijski arhiv ljubljana publishes its books free on matricula, and the parish is there under its own name - kranj-smartin. baptismal index, kranj-smartin 1832-1870 - 104 - martin kozina - 64 , under 1841 born and baptised 16 november 1841 - the same day. the tree had «1841» and nothing more. where oberfeichting, house 9 - zgornje bitnje , a village west of kranj. ehelich / unehelich the tick is in unehelich - born outside marriage . the register has a column for it and the priest used it. vater the column is blank. mutter «gertraud kosina, hublnn. tochter» - a hausler's daughter , the bottom of the land-holding order. godparents lorenz pizz and maria kashar. baptised by blas. ulzhar, coop. two registers, two countries, forty-seven years, and the same absence. kranj, 1841 - vater : blank. mutter : gertraud kosina . senj, 1888 - a dash where the groom's father belongs. «gertruda kozina, posjednica.» the gap in this family tree is not a gap in this family tree. it is what the parish priest wrote down, twice, in two languages, because there was nothing else to write. and she rose. in 1841 she is a cottager's daughter. by 1888 her son describes her to a croatian priest as a posjednica - a property-owner. there is no dagger against her name in 1888 , which suggests she was still living, in her seventies, on the day he married. every other kozina baptism in that book belongs to one household there are five in the whole volume, and all five were opened. baptised house father mother anton 20 jan 1834 oberfeichting 9 johann kosina , hausler lucia labornik petrus 29 jun 1836 oberfeichting 9 johann kosina, hausler lucia labornik martin 16 nov 1841 oberfeichting 9 - none - gertraud kosina , hauslerstochter franz 1853 not checked johann kozina , hausler ursula sedej ana 1856 not checked johann kozina, hausler ursula sedej look at the house column. johann the hausler's two recorded children were born at oberfeichting no. 9 - and five years after the second of them, gertraud bore martin in that same house. that does not tell us whether she was his sister or his daughter. it does tell us she was living in his household , and it turns «a kozina family in the same parish» into one roof . one hausler called johann, two wives, twenty-two years - and in the middle of it one unmarried woman and one child with no father. lucia disappears after 1836; ursula is beside the same husband by 1853. the 1853 and 1856 entries spell the surname kozina with a z , which is the spelling the senj priest reached for in 1888. and what settles it is his marriage. the marriage register for 1816-1855 (sig. 00899) has a column headed «aeltern des brautigams» - the groom's parents . find johann's marriage and you have gertraud's parents too, if she is his sister. the volume carries no index and runs to seventy-seven pages, so it is a scan rather than a lookup, and it is the next thing to do. gertraud is a hauslerstochter - a hausler's daughter - and she stands godmother on page 33. johann is a hausler. father and daughter, or brother and sister, is likely and it is not established , and they stand in the people this tree does not have and nowhere else. two corrections, and they are worth keeping. page 33 on its own read as «josef» ; page 18, with the same wife beside him, reads «johann» , and page 33 at eight times magnification reads johann too - one given name, and a household that would have been split in two . and the 1836 child, taken from the index as «johan» , is «petrus» at the page. that is the third time in two days that an index has been wrong about this family and the register has been right. and then her own baptism was found, by admitting a mistake this page eliminated her, and the elimination was wrong. on 21 september the 1814 candidate was opened and struck out because the father's surname - «franz kosnar, hublar» - ends in a clear «-r» , so it was read as kosnar and not kosina. the letter was read correctly and the conclusion drawn from it was wrong. the «-r» is how that clerk writes this family's name. he writes it the same way for her brother, and her brother's children are entered kosina by the next clerk in the next volume. one family, two hands, and a surname that changes shape between them. the marriage register settled it , because it has a column headed «aeltern des brautigams» . 1833, 6. janner · obern feichting 9 johann kosinar , hausler , katholisch, 30 , ledig × luzia labornik , house 3, 38 , ledig des vaters: franz kosinar, hausler · der mutter: mina tom[sh]shan, hauslerin and the identification does not rest on the surname at all. johann kosina, hausler of oberfeichting no. 9, had his first child with lucia labornik on 20 january 1834 - a year and a fortnight after this wedding . the house, the trade, the wife and the date all agree. his father is franz, a hausler , with a wife written tom[sh]shan - against the 1814 baptism's franz kosinar, hublar and maria do[m]shan . mina is the short form these registers use for marija . the same couple. so the line runs two generations further back franz kosinar × maria «mina» dortschen martin's grandparents - and four generations above hedviga. named in six entries across thirty-three years and never once in person: their own marriage in 1800, four of their children's baptisms, and their son's marriage in 1833. he has a death; she does not. gertraud baptised 18 march 1814 . twenty-seven when she bore martin. johann born about 1802-03 ; married 6 january 1833 ; the hausler of oberfeichting no. 9 . martin born 16 november 1841 at oberfeichting no. 9, unehelich - in his uncle's house . gertraud was not a lodger and not a stranger. she was the householder's sister , and she bore her son under her brother's roof seven years after he brought a wife into it. and then their own marriage, which explains the houses the 1780-1815 marriage book has no index either, so images 30-35 were cropped to the brautigam column and read as strips. it is on image 33, under 1800 . den 27ten [8ber] · feichting b. st. joh. · 10 franz kosinar , katholisch, 24 , ledig × maria dortshen , katholisch, 20 , ledig beystande: matthaus kosinar - signing with a cross - and simon rauth, bauern . married by matthaus lauts, coop. 27 october 1800 , at twenty-four and twenty. so franz was born about 1776 and maria about 1780 . the two house numbers, and a first answer that did not survive. this page had said the numbers were «not tight» - gertraud baptised at house 10, johann marrying into house 9 - and on 22 september it explained them as «house 10 is the parents', house 9 is the brother's» . that was wrong, and the register said so the same evening. franz's own children are baptised at house 9 in 1812 , at house 10 in 1814 and 1815 , and at oberfeichting 9 again in 1820 - where the clerk writes him haubler , the man of the house. both houses were his at different times , and the family moved between them. the explanation is kept here, struck through, because it is a fair example of how quickly a tidy answer can be built on two data points. a third kosinar - and for one day nobody could say what he was. matthaus kosinar stood witness and signed with a cross, because he could not write . a man of the same surname witnessing for a twenty-four-year-old groom is most likely his father or his brother, and this page said for a day that nothing here says which . his death says which. mrliska knjiga 1812-1835, book p. 64: «1819, den 16ten april · ober-feichting · 14 · matthaus kosina · keischler · alter 45 · rothlauf und brand» . forty-five in 1819 is born about 1774. franz was born 1775-76. two men born a year apart are not father and son - so the man who could not sign his name in 1800 was franz's brother, and he was twenty-six when he stood up for him. and the 1818 candidate is settled rather than merely moot. her unreadable father - «lukas ko[s]in…» , house 12 - is on image 31 of this same book: «lukas kosina, katholisch, 29, ledig», married 1799 , so born about 1770. a real man and a different household. the 1814 gertraud is left with no rival. the mother's surname, from six clerks across thirty-three years. «dortshen» 1800 · «dortschen» 1812 · «do[m]shan» 1814 · «dortschen» 1815 · «dortschen» 1820 · «tom[sh]shan» 1833. four of the six read dortschen , and the two that do not are this archive's own bracketed readings of a hand it found hard. on 22 september 2026 this page changed its lead spelling to «dortschen» and kept all six. mina is the short form these registers use for marija , and one clerk writes marina . and one rung further up is a wall, for now franz's own baptism is not in this parish. he was twenty-four in october 1800, so born between late 1775 and late 1776. the baptismal register was walked from october 1775 to january 1777 - ten openings, every infans and parentes column - and there is no kosinar in it at all . the absence says something , because the same surname is all over the same register fifty years later: johann's children in 1834, 1836, 1853 and 1856, and gertraud's martin in 1841. in the mid-1770s it is simply not there. he came from elsewhere he married into feichting house 10 at twenty-four, which is what a man who marries a household does - and it would make the kosinar of kranj-smartin his descendants rather than his ancestors . matthaus the witness cuts against it, and proves nothing either way. the age is wrong «24» in a marriage register is very often a round number. the name is unreadable the 1770s hand may write the surname unrecognisably - which it already proved to do in 1814 , when «kosinar» was read as «kosnar» and a real candidate was struck out on this very page. so the death register was opened, and it confirmed him the death index is letter-tabbed, and the whole k section for 1836-1869 holds exactly two kozina . 22. - 24. [janner 1849] · ob. feichtg · 9 franz kosina , ausnehmer · katholisch · mannlich · alter 73 · lungenentzundung · versehen aged 73 in january 1849 - born 1775-76 , which independently confirms the «24» he gave at his own wedding forty-nine years earlier. two records, two clerks, one birth year. and it means the missing baptism really is missing , rather than the age being wrong. one word in that entry tells you what happened to the house. he is an ausnehmer : a householder who has handed over and lives out his life on the ausnahm , the retirement provision written into the transfer. he died at oberfeichting 9 - the house he himself held in 1820 , that his son johann was keeping by 1833 , and that his grandson martin was born in in 1841 . he did not move in with his son. he gave his son the house and stayed in it. 30. - 2. xbr [1850] · ob. feichtg · 9 luzia kosina , hublersweib · weiblich · alter 55 · lungenentzundung · versehen · jos. kartely lucia labornik. aged 55 in november 1850, so born about 1795 - and she was 38 at her marriage in january 1833 , which gives 1794-95. the same woman. she is entered a hublers- weib and not a widow, which is right, because johann outlived her. and it answers a question this page had left hanging: why johann is beside ursula sedej by 1853. because lucia died in 1850 - in the same house and of the same pneumonia as his father, twenty-two months apart. maria is not there. the k section for 1836-1869 has franz and luzia and nobody else . so the earlier index - 1812-1835 - had to be read, and on 22 september 2026 it was, end to end. it did not give her. it gave five other people. the scans are the archdiocese's, not ours , so they are transcribed here and linked rather than republished - index sig. 04632 image 246, register sig. 00886 image 65, at data.matricula-online.eu . mrliska knjiga kranj-smartin 1812-1835 · page 34 the page we went to find one woman on, and found two the index for 1812-1835 lists «kozina maria - 34» under the year 1816. page 34 is the left leaf of the eighteenth opening, and the year is written across the top of it. it carries two maria kozinar, four weeks apart, and neither of them is martin's grandmother. den 27 [februar 1816] · z[ubern] · 4 maria kozinar , haubl. · katholisc 

s: One page of a parish register closes the gap this archive was built around, and opens a marriage nobody in it knew about
q: the wedding of 1920 one page of a parish register closes the gap this archive was built around, and opens a marriage nobody in it knew about senj, 8 december 1920 - entry 41, page 366 the wedding of 1920 one page of a parish register closes the gap this archive was built around, and opens a marriage nobody in it knew about. the first build of this archive said that the join at generation three rested on no document at all . it rested on one the whole time - attached in the family tree, absent from the gedcom export, and never read. senj, roman catholic marriage register ( vjencani ), page 366, entry 41. the relevant row is boxed in red on the scan as it is held in the tree. what the entry records date 8 prosinca (december) 1920 , at senj groom ljubomir blazevic , mornar - sailor . born rijeka , resident senj , roman catholic, born 1892, 1/iii - 1 march 1892. status: neozenjen , bachelor. bride milka vukelic , radnica u tvornici duhana - worker in the tobacco factory . born senj , resident senj, roman catholic, born 1886, 9/x - 9 october 1886. status: udova - widow. groom's parents juraj blazevic and tereza r. zubrinic , annotated mrt. - deceased bride's parents josip papic and antonija r. prpic witnesses franjo bora- , brijac - barber - whose surname runs into the column rule and is not read here ; and vinko tijan , cinovnik u tvornici duhana - a clerk in the tobacco factory priest ivan vidas , parohijalni administrator remarks dispensed by the ordinariate, act no. 3371 of 4 december ; banns read three times ; married u stolnoj crkvi - in the cathedral read again at full resolution, 13 september 2026. the copy held in the tree is 960 pixels wide. the same opening was fetched from familysearch at 5,812 × 4,273 - image 371 of the senj marriage film, 3:1:3qsq-g99x-17m7 - which is where the witnesses, the priest and the dispensation number above come from. nothing already on this page changed except that "tereza r. zubrinic" can now be read with its caron . question 5c → the thing this page exists for generation three is now documented the register names the groom's father and mother: juraj blazevic and tereza nee zubrinic . that is exactly the link this archive marked as disputed - the join on which generations four to eight all hang. it is a good witness. a marriage entry is written by the parish priest at the time, from the couple in front of him, with the banns and a dispensation recorded in the margin. it is not a later reconstruction, and it has no interest in anybody's pedigree. what it does not do. it names juraj - it does not date him, place him, or name his father. the wall simply moves up one generation: the link from ljubomir to juraj is now evidenced; the link from juraj to toma is still not. open questions → three things nobody had recorded milka had been married before she marries in 1920 under the name vukelic , and her status is udova - widow . the family tree carries her only as milka papic, wife of ljubomir. the media library holds a photograph captioned "zvonomir and milka marriage" , and hedviga's own list of immediate family on myheritage includes a miroslava "mica" vukelic (1907-1993) . a first husband named vukelic and a daughter born in 1907 fit together, and would make miroslava hedviga's half-sister . stated here as an inference - the first marriage record has not been read. she was on the factory floor in 1920 milka is radnica - a worker - in the tobacco factory . the tree records her as supervisor of workers at the same factory. both are true, thirty years apart: this is a documented promotion, and the only career progression visible anywhere in this archive. senj and the factory → juraj was already dead the groom's parents carry the annotation mrt. - deceased. tereza zubrinic is recorded in the tree as dying in 1931 , eleven years after this entry, so the note is most consistent with applying to juraj alone - giving him a death before december 1920 , the first date of any kind attached to him. if instead it covers both parents, then the tree's date for tereza is wrong. either way something has been learned, and it is worth resolving. and it confirms the sailor the tree gives ljubomir's occupation as mornar / fisherman . the register, in 1920, says mornar - sailor. confirmed from the record rather than from family memory. a discrepancy worth keeping the register says ljubomir was born 1 march 1892 . his gravestone at senj says 1891 . the register wins. it was written in 1920 by a priest copying from a baptismal certificate, while the stone was cut after 1966 by people working from memory and from whatever the family then believed. this archive records the birth as 1 march 1892 and records the stone as wrong - which is worth saying out loud, because a gravestone looks like the most authoritative source in genealogy and frequently is not.

q: method every claim here carries a confidence. the point of saying so is that a reader can disagree with the reasoning instead o how to read anything on this site method every claim here carries a confidence. the point of saying so is that a reader can disagree with the reasoning instead of having to take the conclusion on trust. the five words all seven of these family archives grade a claim with the same five words, so a level means the same thing wherever you meet it. the word is always printed next to the colour, because a reader should never have to know the palette to know the confidence. documented a record was read, and it says this. the source is named. probable the evidence points one way and nothing found so far points the other. not proven. inferred reasoned from what is known - a gap of the right size, a name in the right place - rather than witnessed in a record. family told, remembered, or written on a family chart. kept, because discarding it would lose the lead; labelled, because it is not evidence. disputed two sources disagree and neither has been ruled out. both are shown. not claimed some pages carry this instead. it states the thing a reader is likely to assume - the connection that would be tidy, the identification that almost works - and says plainly that this archive does not assert it. an archive is judged as much by what it refuses to say as by what it says. the five labels documented a named source with a reference, and where possible the scan. the strongest things in this archive are the familysearch citations into the croatian parish registers - senj, krivi put, otocac, karlobag - which give an image group, a page and a date. inferred a reasoned conclusion from documented facts, with the reasoning written out so it can be overturned. that the family is bunjevac is an inference from place and surname, not a statement in any record. superseded asserted in the family record, and now displaced by a document that says otherwise. disputed asserted in the family record but unsupported, or contradicted, by what can be seen - like the join at generation three . family lore told, remembered, not corroborated. kept because it is precious; labelled because pretending otherwise is how family myths become family history. both accounts of oto's death sit here. the rule that governs the whole build living people are not here they are not hidden, not gated, not present in the output. the rule is applied once, in classify_living() , at the boundary between the research data and the published site. because thousands of people in a tree this size carry no dates at all, judging each by their own record alone marks every one of them living - safe, but useless. so the build computes an upper bound on each person's birth year from their own events, their children's births, their marriages and their parents' bounds, and publishes somebody only when even the latest year they could have been born is more than a century ago. a recorded birth or christening → born in that year, exactly any recorded event in year e → born no later than e a child born in year c → born no later than c - 14 a marriage in year m → born no later than m - 14 a parent whose bound is p → born no later than p + 60 every step is a real bound, never a guess, and a recorded birth is never overridden by inference. on the current export that judges 2,034 of 15,643 people living. a living spouse, parent or child is not named on anybody else's page either. a removal request is honoured within days, without argument and without requiring a reason. this is stricter than its sister archives, and the difference is deliberate. the defranceschi archive publishes living people by name only - no dates, no places, no photographs , and the falco archive moved to the same rule in september 2026, naming 104 of them. this archive names none of its 2,034 . two reasons, and only one of them is principle. the scale is different - 2,034 living people against falco's 104 - and a rule that is comfortable for a hundred relatives is a different proposition for two thousand. and this archive is about one woman who died in 2001 : almost nothing it argues depends on anybody alive. where a living person is the only link in a chain, the page says "living, withheld" and the chain is shown broken rather than quietly completed. it is a divergence, not an oversight , and it is written here so that a reader moving between the family sites is not left wondering which rule is in force. an online family tree is a witness, not a source the spine here is a myheritage tree of 15,643 people . most "sources" attached to people in it are other trees - geni world family tree , boras web site , grlica web site , janicic , marko karic rodoslov . when four trees agree, that is four witnesses who may all have copied one another; it is not four documents. so the register page marks only whether a person carries any source string at all, and every person page prints the strings verbatim so a reader can see what kind of thing is being relied on. where a citation points at a parish register image , that is the one worth going to. sources → two things this archive does to the data, and admits to it folds spellings zubrinic, zubrinic, zubrinich, xubrinich and xubrinic are counted as one name ; so are prpic and perpic. without that, the family fragments into eight small families that appear unrelated. the folding is done in one function so it can be inspected and argued with. why the spellings differ → it drops the working scaffolding the tree contains sorting stubs - "senj - unknown to be sorted papic" , "brothers [of stephanus] zubrinic" , "nn blazevic" . these are research notes, not people, and publishing them as ancestors would be a lie. they are filtered by name pattern at the build boundary. what is not committed the raw gedcom is not published - it contains every living person in full. it is kept out of any public copy of this repository and regenerated from a fresh myheritage export when needed.

q: milka hedviga's mother is the best-documented person in this archive: a birth entry, two marriage entries, a gravestone and a senj, 9 october 1886 - 7 september 1971 milka hedviga's mother is the best-documented person in this archive: a birth entry, two marriage entries, a gravestone and a factory. her life can be told almost entirely from records, and it is not the life the family tree describes. the tree carries milka lucia papic as the wife of ljubomir blazevic and the mother of seven. the registers carry a woman who was married twice , widowed at twenty-eight , and spent more than forty years in the same tobacco factory - going in as a floor worker and coming out supervising it. senj baptisms, page 122, entry 96 born 9 october 1886 senj, roman catholic baptisms, str. 122 , entry 96. her entry is the second from the bottom of the left-hand page. name milka lucia - zakonita , legitimate born / baptised 9 october 1886 , baptised 17 october father josip papic , trhonosa - a load-carrier mother tonka rod. prpic godparents josip glavicic , also a trhonosa , and ivka filipovic baptised by the chaplain ( kapelan ) at senj later annotation the margin was written up again when she died - the register records the death entry and the date 7.9.1971 , endorsed at senj 30.9.1971 . a small correction. the family tree gives her baptism as 19 october . the register says 17 . the archive follows the register. both her father and her godfather are trhonose - men who carried other people's goods on their backs for a fee. that is not a coincidence; it is a social world. in a port town whose port had died, the porters knew the porters . senj marriages, page 294, entry 30 first marriage, 4 november 1907 aged twenty-one, she married zvonimir m. vukelic - and nothing in the family tree's account of her had ever mentioned it. senj marriages, page 294, entry 30, boxed in red on the scan as held in the tree. date 4 studenoga (november) 1907 , senj groom zvonimir m. vukelic , gostionicarski pomocnik - innkeeper's assistant . born 13 january 1883 . bachelor. bride milka papic , radnica u tvornici duhana - a worker in the tobacco factory. born 9 october 1886. unmarried. his parents vukelic pl. petar , gostionicar - innkeeper - and † vjekoslava , surname read as putnic (possibly putinic - not settled) . the dagger stands before vjekoslava, not before petar: it is the mother who was dead in 1907. her parents joso papic, gostionicar and tonka rod. prpic witnesses koloman pl. vukelic , mestar u tvornici duhana - master in the tobacco factory, not a broker - and franjo olivieri , trgovac , merchant banns married by episcopal dispensation , with the banns read once - on 3 november , the day before the wedding - instead of the usual three times read again at full resolution, 13 september 2026 - and three things on this table changed. the copy held in the tree is 960 pixels wide; the same opening was fetched from familysearch at 5,812 × 4,273 (image 299, 3:1:3qs7-l99x-175j ). this page had petar vukelic marked deceased and his wife as vica . the register reads "vukelic pl. petar gostionicar, i † vjekoslava putnic" - the cross belongs to vjekoslava , and her name is not vica. and koloman was called a broker here; the word is mestar , master - a grade this archive already maps on the factory ladder . what did not change: both vukelic men carry pl. , milka is already a tobacco-factory worker in 1907, and her birth is written 1886, 9/10 - which her 1920 entry repeats as 9/x , thirteen years apart in two different hands. what changed → her father has changed trade. in 1886 josip papic is a trhonosa . by 1907 the register calls him gostionicar - an innkeeper. the tree lists his occupations as " trhonosa, bremenar, gostionicar ", and the registers show that string is a sequence : the porter kept the money and bought a bar. and the middle term now has its own document. his own marriage entry - senj, 3 may 1885 , read at full size the same day - enters him as bremenar , and the 1891 baptism of a child calls him tezak . four documents, four points on one line: trhonosa 1886 · bremenar 1885 · tezak 1891 · gostionicar 1907 . the papici → the one-day dispensation is worth noticing without over-reading. her daughter miroslava was born in 1907 . a hurried wedding and a child in the same year is a familiar shape, but the register does not date the birth and this archive does not claim to know which came first. two children, and a widow at twenty-eight the vukelic children miroslava "mica" / "nana" vukelic (1907-1993), who married rahamin levi (1904-1984) of pirot ; and josip vukelic (1913-2004), born at senj. they are hedviga's half-brother and half-sister , and they were in the tree all along - invisible to the first build of this archive only because a sweep of somebody's ancestors never walks sideways. 1915 zvonimir vukelic died in 1915 , aged thirty-two, in the middle of the first world war. milka was twenty-eight , with a girl of eight and a boy of two. nothing in this archive says how he died, and 1915 is a year in which a man of thirty-two might die many ways. open questions → senj marriages, page 366, entry 41 second marriage, 8 december 1920 thirteen years after the first wedding and five years after the death, she married ljubomir blazevic , a sailor. the register enters her under her married name: milka vukelic, udova - widow. she is still radnica u tvornici duhana . thirteen years on from her first marriage entry, the same job, the same words. the full entry → seven children followed, of whom hedviga was the fourth, born 3 august 1926 - and oto , who did not come home from the war. the factory, over a lifetime 1907, aged 21 radnica u tvornici duhana - worker , per the marriage register 1920, aged 34 radnica u tvornici duhana - still a worker , per the marriage register later supervisor of workers at the cigarette factory, per the family tree - at ul. stjepana radica 4 , "now a textile factory" and beside her anka blazevic (1893-1953), her husband's sister, a radnica in the same factory this is the only career progression documented anywhere in this archive, and it belongs to a woman. in a town where the men are recorded as day labourers, porters and sailors, the steady wage was hers . why there was no other work → 7 september 1971 she died at senj, aged eighty-four, and is on the family stone as milka blazevic rod. papic ✳ 1886 † 1971 - under her maiden name, not the vukelic name she carried into her second wedding, and beside the son whose body was never found. the grave → what is still missing. zvonimir vukelic's death entry for 1915, which would say how she was widowed; miroslava's 1907 birth entry, which would fix the order of wedding and child; and any record of what milka did between 1915 and 1920, alone with two children in a town with no work.

q: the names blazevic is the seventeenth commonest surname in croatia. zubrinic is held by about three hundred people on earth. both four surnames, one of them almost extinct the names blazevic is the seventeenth commonest surname in croatia. zubrinic is held by about three hundred people on earth. both are in this family, and the rare one is the one that travels. what they mean blazevic - "son of blaz" a patronymic from the given name blaz , the croatian form of blasius / blaise, itself from latin blaesus , "lisping" or "stammering". the suffix -evic / -ic is the ordinary south slavic "child of". it is the 17th most frequent surname in croatia . its densest counties are split-dalmatia, virovitica-podravina and osijek-baranja - not lika-senj. our blazevici sit outside the name's main clusters, which is a caution: sharing this surname with someone is nearly meaningless as evidence. zubrinic - the rare one about 312 bearers worldwide , of whom 292 are in croatia at a density of 1:14,482. within croatia its two great concentrations are the city of zagreb (28%) and lika-senj county (25%) - and lika-senj is where tereza and her forebears at otocac are from. a name this rare behaves in the opposite way to blazevic: two zubrinici in the otocac registers are probably related. that makes it the most useful surname in this archive. papic - "son of the priest", or of papa from pop / papa - priest. the tree itself preserves the alternate form: seventy-nine of its papici are written papic (papa) , and the direct ancestor is recorded as "georgius juraj (joannis) papa 'jure' antic papic" - carrying antic and papic at once. the family was changing its name in the record, in front of us. prpic - and perpic a hypocoristic patronymic, from a short form of a given name. in this tree it is written prpic 83 times, perpic 19, perpic 16, prpic 8 - and one record hedges openly as "papic or perpic" . antonija herself is entered as "perpic / prpic" . prpic concentrates in zagreb (27%), primorje-gorski kotar (17%) and lika-senj (13%) - again the family's own ground. the most important thing on this page x wrote the sound z the zubrinic name appears in this tree in eight different spellings , and they are not errors. they are three successive orthographies for one unchanged spoken name. xubrinich the venetian-italian convention used along this coast, in which x stood for the sound written z in modern croatian, and -ch for -c . latin-language parish registers in habsburg croatia use it constantly. zubrinich the german-latin compromise of the imperial administration: the diacritic dropped because the clerk's alphabet had no way to write it, the -ich ending kept. zubrinic modern croatian , after gaj's diacritical reform of the 1830s made z and c standard. this is the form the family uses today. the direct ancestors are entered under both at once - nicolaus "nikola" zubrinic (xubrinic) , born at otocac on 24 january 1834, and his father michael "mate" zubrinic / zubrinic / xubrinich , born 1811. whoever built this tree was reading across all three systems, which is the right instinct. the practical consequence. searching croatian records for zubrinic alone will miss most of the family before about 1850. the name has to be searched as xubrinich , zubrinich , xubrinic and zubrinic as well - and this archive's own tooling folds all of them to one key before it counts anything. the surname is only half the problem the given names change language too these registers were kept in latin , and then in croatian . the same man is joannes in the book that baptised him and ivan in the one that married him - and a fair number of entries decline him into joannem or joannis , because a priest writing baptizavi josephum is writing the accusative, not the name. so the archive's own register was splitting people from themselves . a reader searching ivan was shown 42 of them and not the other 46 . of 34 canonical given names in registers are narrative latin , not forms. a priest writes baptizavi josephum - "i baptised josephus" - and filius josephi - "son of josephus". those endings are grammar . transcribed literally into a family tree, they become names, and the tree acquires a man called josephum who was never called that by anyone. 47 of the people published here carry one - 20 genitives, 18 accusatives, one dative georgij genitive two parishes, three priests, three decades apart. in the 1806 book every child on the page is named in the accusative - mariam, joannem, matthaeam, magdalenam, vincentium, nicolaum. that is not a slip anyone made; it is how the sentence works. baptizavi infantem … nomine josephum - the child is the grammatical object of the verb, so the child's name takes the object's ending. and karlobag settles it from a single hand. one priest, joannes antonius ivankovich , writing in the same book four years apart: 1777 cui impositum est nomen joannis georgij genitive 1781 cui impositum est nomen oliva maria nominative the same formula, the same parish, the same man - and a different case each time. a third karlobag priest, michael martinaz, writes nomen caetani antonij in 1779. it is not a rule and it is not an error: it is scribal caprice , and a tree that copies the word faithfully inherits whichever case the priest happened to use that morning. which makes the ending useful. if the case is the register's own grammar rather than an error, it records how that person appeared in the entry they were found in : accusative - josephum , mariam - they were the one being baptised. the entry is their own . genitive or dative - joannis , pauli , simoni - they were named as somebody's parent. the entry belongs to their child , and they appear only in passing. so the six ancestors carrying a genitive are people this archive has never yet seen a record of - only records that mention them. that is a reading list, not a defect. what would close them → and the registers underline the by-names. the 1806 vrbnik scribe rules a line under a second name after the surname - antich papa , loncsarich franich , antich dudin , pobor rataj . these are nadimci , house by-names that tell one household from another where a whole village shares a surname - the same problem the house numbers solve. it also puts a documented papa beside the 79 people this tree writes papic (papa) , and leaves an open question: whether that is the by-name of an antic household rather than a surname in its own right. the papic line → nothing has been renamed. the tree is the authority on what the tree says, and this archive's job is to note where what it says is a grammatical artefact rather than to quietly correct it - the person pages carry the note, and the search folds the forms together so that josephum and josip find each other. read this before you search the name what the surname-origin websites say about zubrinic is invented because zubrinic is rare, it is exactly the kind of name that the automated "meaning and origin of your surname" sites fill in with confident fiction. one of them, consulted for this archive, produced the following - and it is worth setting out, because somebody researching this family will find it. "a croatian ban" it names "petar zubrinic, an 18th-century croatian ban" . the bans of croatia in that century were palffy, draskovic, eszterhazy, branyng, batthyany, nadasdy, esterhazy, balassa and erdody . there was no ban zubrinic. the claim is fabricated. two etymologies the same site derives the name from zubor , "babble" - a talkative man - and from zubr / zubr , the aurochs . these are unrelated words. it concedes the second is " nije potvrdeno ", unconfirmed, having just asserted the first. the wrong region it states the name "originates from dalmatia and is most prevalent there today". the distribution figures below put 25% of croatian bearers in lika-senj and 28% in the city of zagreb - the usual modern drift to a capital - and dalmatia nowhere . this family's own records run through otocac , in lika, for two centuries. noble status asserted for the 17th century, with no document, by a source that has already invented a viceroy. what can honestly be said is small. the name is a standard -ic patronymic built on a stem zubr- ; which personal name or nickname stands behind that stem is a question for croatian onomastic scholarship, and this archive has not found an authority that answers it. everything else on this page is counted, not guessed. method → the general lesson is worth more than the particular one. a surname-origin website that cites nothing is not a weak source; it is not a source. the safe test is the one applied here: take its single most checkable factual claim - a named person holding a named office in a named century - and check it. and then the name emigrates when the family leaves, the spelling forks permanently - and the two forks can be counted separately. form bearers where they are zubrinic - the homeland form 312 croatia 292, serbia 14, montenegro 6. 100% in europe. zubrinic - the diaspora form 69 argentina 29, canada 16, united states 8, south africa 7 , netherlands 5. none in croatia at all. the two lists do not overlap by a single country. the diacritics are not decoration; q: open questions written down so they can be worked on, and so no reader mistakes a gap for a fact. each one says what would actually clo 19 open · 9 answered open questions written down so they can be worked on, and so no reader mistakes a gap for a fact. each one says what would actually close it. the most valuable thing anyone can send this archive is a correction . the second most valuable is a document that closes one of these. each question is in four parts - what is known, what has been tried, and the record that would settle it. the middle one is the part most archives leave out, and it is the part that stops the same dead end being walked twice. show all 28 answered 9 substantive 5 worth doing 7 critical 4 data quality 3 1 who were ljubomir's parents? answered what is known this was the archive's central doubt: the join at generation three rested on a man with no document. the senj marriage register of 8 december 1920 names the groom's parents outright - juraj blazevic and tereza r. zubrinic - and confirms ljubomir's birth as 1 march 1892. what has been tried it was attached in the family tree the whole time and absent from the gedcom export, which is why the archive spent its first weeks treating a documented join as an open doubt. what would settle it nothing further. what replaces it is question 1b. the 1920 register → 1b who was juraj blazevic's father? - a house number, and a second witness substantive what is known four more registers were read in september 2026 and the man is no longer a bare name. he has an occupation and a house. his son marijan's baptism, 12 april 1895 , enters him as "jurko blazevic i tereza rod. zubrinic, selj. " - peasant - living at smokvica kbr. 114 . and a second register names the couple. anka blazevic's marriage to pavao kosina on 20 november 1919 gives her parents as juraj blazevic i tereza r. zubrinic - independently of the 1920 entry for their son ljubomir. and the house is now written out in full. antonija "tonka" blazevic's marriage to ginro babic on 1 december 1912 enters her parents as "††toma i tereza blazevic, poljodjelci iz sela smokvica kbr. 114 " - not a number in a baptismal margin but the household stated in plain croatian, both of them marked dead. that is a fourth independent document for house 114 and the first to name toma and tereza together with the number. it hardens the household the whole argument stands on; it still does not name juraj's father. and the godparents close the circle. the tree gives juraj two younger siblings, marija (b. 1880) and ivan (b. 1882) - children of toma at house 114. the godparents at marijan's 1895 baptism are entered as "ive blazevic, sin tomin " and "marija blazevic, cer tomina " : the son and the daughter of a toma, of the right names and the right ages, standing for the child of the man who lives in toma's house. with the house number demoted to a kin-group, the godparents carry the weight - and they carry it well. godparents are chosen , and a man's own brother and sister are the classic choice. what has been tried the house turned out to be a zadruga, not a household - this archive's own correction. toma and terezija pecanic are recorded at smokvica 114 in 1882 and 1884 , and toma was born at br. 114 in 1838. but a control document - the 1890 baptism of frane blazevic - puts pavao blazevic, son of luka , at smokvica 114 as well. luka and toma's father anton are both sons of ilija , so pavao and toma are first cousins, and the number covers an extended-family compound . it places juraj in ilija's kin-group; it cannot name his father. the zadruga → september 2026 - and the patronymic turns out to be deliberate. reading the 1888 baptism of pavao's daughter terezija, also at smokvica 114, gives a godfather called ivo blazevic sin matin - son of mate . so two different men named ivo blazevic stood godfather at this one house within seven years , told apart only by their fathers' names. that is why the priest bothered with a patronymic at all: there were several ivo blazevici about, and "sin tomin" in 1895 is a distinction he chose to draw, not a formula. it also shows the compound from the outside - one house number holding toma's children, pavao's children, jurko's children, an ivo son of toma and an ivo son of mate. september 2026 - and the godparent column says it plainly. four baptisms at smokvica 114 have now been read, and the godparents are drawn from two distinct blazevic sibling-sets : 1888 ivo blazevic sin matin · anica tomljanovic 1894 sime pecanic · mara blazevic matina 1895 ive blazevic sin tomin · marija blazevic cer tomina 1896 nikola blazevic · ana krpan kci ilijina mate's children and toma's children, both standing at the same house, plus a pecanic - toma's wife's family. that is what a zadruga looks like from the godparent column : one number, several fathers, and the children of one brother standing for the children of another. it still does not name jurko's father; it does make the compound something you can see rather than infer. what would settle it it is still not the sentence that says so. what would give it: jurko's own baptism in the sv. jakov krmpote register, or his marriage to tereza zubrinic before 1892. two of his children, marijan (1895) and ruza (1897) , have no marriage recorded anywhere - and every marriage entry re-names the parents, so those are two more chances at the same answer. 1c who was milka's first husband? answered what is known zvonimir m. vukelic , gostionicarski pomocnik - innkeeper's assistant - born 13 january 1883, married at senj on 4 november 1907 (marriages p.294 no.30 - read at full resolution 13 september 2026, image 299 of the film). he died in 1915 , aged thirty-two, leaving milka a widow at twenty-eight. their children miroslava "mica" vukelic (1907-1993) and josip vukelic (1913-2004) are hedviga's half-sister and half-brother - and were in the tree all along. what would settle it nothing further on identity. what remains is 1d. milka's life → 1d how did zvonimir vukelic die in 1915? - and a correction worth doing what is known his baptism has been read: born 13 january 1883 at senj, baptised 25 february, son of petar pl. vukelic - plemeniti , noble - and lojza. milka married into a titled family and was widowed out of it at twenty-eight. and a third occupation, from a third document. on 16 august 1914 he stands witness at the wedding of milka's sister franjka, entered as "zvonko m. vukelic, pivar " - brewer. the trajectory now reads gostionicarski pomocnik (1907) → pivar (1914) → gostionicar, bankar (at death). it is also the first document found that places him inside this family other than his own marriage entry. what has been tried this archive proposed the austro-hungarian casualty lists, reasoning that he was thirty-two in the second year of the war. that reasoning was probably wrong. the tree places his death at senj , in his own town, and gives his occupation as gostionicar, bankar - innkeeper and banker , a considerable rise from the gostionicarski pomocnik who married milka in 1907. a man who dies at home, in a settled trade, is not a verlustliste entry. what would settle it the senj death register for 1915 , and nothing else. the casualty lists are behind a subscription for uncommon surnames and are, on this evidence, the wrong book. 1e which came first - the wedding or the child? worth doing what is known milka and zvonimir married on 4 november 1907 by episcopal dispensation, with the banns read once on 3 november rather than three times. their daughter miroslava was born in 1907 . a dispensation, a one-day wedding and a child in the same year make a familiar shape - but the register does not date the birth, and this archive does not claim to know. what has been tried weakened 13 september 2026. the senj marriage of martin kosina and angjelika boras, 12 january 1888 , carries the same shape: dispensed by the senj ordinariate on 7 january, banns read once only on the 8th, married on the 12th. he was 47 and she 30 , and there is no suggestion of anything in it. a single dispensation in this diocese looks like ordinary administrative practice, not evidence - so this question rests on the birth date alone, and that is exactly what is missing. what would settle it miroslava vukelic's baptismal entry, senj 1907 , which gives the day. 2 how did oto blazevic die? critical the spine depends on it. what is known two accounts in the same note, from two named relatives: a snakebite , and killed in the war in slavonia with no known grave . a photograph of the family grave now corroborates the second witness in its checkable parts - oto's name is on the stone, and leo and katica were added later exactly as she described. it still does not establish the cause . what would settle it a search of the yugoslav war victims register ( popis zrtava rata ) and croatian state archives military death records for oto blazevic, b. 1923, senj . an entry - or a confirmed absence - settles it. the full page → 3 when did santou codron leave rhodes? substantive what is known born on rhodes in 1913 ; alive in south africa to marry hedviga about 1973 . the island's jewish community was deported on 23 july 1944 and roughly 150 of 1,615 survived. whether he left before the war - as ~2,000 rhodes jews did, for the congo and rhodesia - or survived the deportation is not known here , and the difference is enormous. what would settle it south african immigration and naturalisation papers giving arrival year and last residence; the rhodes jewish museum community registers and yad vashem deportation lists, searched for codron. the full page → 4 is the port pirie branch the same zubrinic family? critical the spine depends on it. what is known now traceable three generations back from the emigrant: ivan zubrinic (1860-1930) → his father joannes, b. 19 june 1837, forest ranger → elias "ilija" (1806-1845) → casparus (1767-1829) . and there it stops: in the tree, casparus's parent is a node literally named "brothers of casparus (it seems) zubrinic" - a researcher's guess written into the structure. nothing joins the two lines - and as of 13 september 2026 it is possible to say exactly what the apparent join is made of. walk casparus upward and the chain reads: casparus 1767 → "brothers of casparus (it seems)" → "c zubrinic xubrinich zubrinic" → "zubrinic zubrinix xubrinic zubrinic otocac" . the second is a researcher's note. the third is an alphabet - one of eighteen nodes whose entire given name is a single letter, holding everyone whose name starts with it. ninety-two people are attached that way. walk toma upward and he stops at a bare node called zubrinic after one step. so the two lines meet in a filing system and nowhere else. but they are born a year apart in one small village. casparus 14 january 1767; toma 1768, at sumecica 2 - and the 1834 frontier baptism this archive has read is at sumecica 24 . a surname held by ~312 people on earth, two men born a year apart in the same hamlet. the frontier → what has been tried the 1760s baptisms do not exist in any collection reachable from here - checked 13 september 2026. familysearch's otocac holdings begin in 1834 . this question's stated next step has been unavailable the whole time, and better image access does not change that. the same parish holds a better document, and this archive had never looked at it. church census (stanje dusa) 1710-1846 - a status animarum , filmed at the croatian state archives as otocac knj. 1 , 384 images. it is not a register of events but a standing list of households , and its columns are the ones this question actually needs: pagus the village domus the house number nomina familiae every member, relationship spelled out dies/mensis/annus a birth date for each a baptism register would give two fathers' names. this book would give the house - and for a question about whether two men born a year apart in one hamlet belong to one zadruga , the house is the better answer. it covers 1767 and 1768. what it was judged to cost. it is not in familysearch's full-text index - tested, the query returns nothing - and there is no index at the front of the book. the pagus is written sideways in the gutter and vanishes into the binding shadow on many frames, so on a first sitting it could not even be navigated by village reliably. that meant about 110 openings read one at a time , looking for zubrinic in the name column and sumecica in the margin. a sitting, not a lookup - but a sitting that could actually be taken. 14 september 2026 - the census was read, and it does not hold this family. the pagus margin turned out to be perfectly legible: the village is written bottom-to-top in the gutter, so the earlier sitting's rotation rendered it upside down. rotated the other way, twenty-two openings gave the village order of the whole book - ottosaz · luka · dubrava · novoselia · lieska · kostelievo selo · obilje · beljue · shumechicza · luka · extinctae - and put sumecica at images 102-106. five openings, not a hundred and ten. all five were read. the households are dasovic (domus 9), stabincic (10), orehovic (4) , a paulus household, a household of andreas and stephanus, janezic, ollar, kovacic, orehovacki . there is no zubrinic at sumecica in this book, and no domus 2 and no domus 24. the extinctae section was read too; the ruled census stops about image 112 and what follows has no pagus column at all. the likeliest reading is that the sumecica block was written once, early, and never re-made - its households carry births into the 1840s because members were added to existing families, not because new families were entered. and there is outside support for that: the 1913 hungarian gazetteer gives sumecica a population of 200 , and degen's flora velebitica calls it a hausergruppe , a group of houses south-west of otocac. two hundred people is roughly twenty-five households against the census's seven or eight. the book is not the whole village. notes/otocac-status-animarum.md and a warning about the other book on the same film. the otocac marriage register 1859-18

q: the brother hedviga's brother died at twenty-two in the last year of the war. the family preserves two accounts of how, they cannot oto blazevic, 1923-1945 the brother hedviga's brother died at twenty-two in the last year of the war. the family preserves two accounts of how, they cannot both be true, and there is no grave to ask. this page exists because the record contains a contradiction that has been kept rather than tidied away . both accounts are written into the same note on oto's entry, attributed to two different people, and this archive reproduces them exactly as they stand. the first account bitten by snake - attributed in the tree to ivan defranceski ivan anton defranceski (1925-1995) was hedviga's husband and oto's brother-in-law - two years younger than oto, and alive in the same town at the time. the velebit has the horned viper , vipera ammodytes , europe's most dangerous snake, and a shepherd or a labourer on that mountain was genuinely at risk. the second account the late otto blazevic was the brother of ljuba, leo, aunt karma, aunt seka … he died in the war somewhere in slavonia , his grave is unknown, so they put his name in his grandmother's and grandfather's grave - and now leo is there, and katica. - attributed in the tree to nives blazevic this one names his siblings correctly, including "aunt seka" - hedviga's own nickname - which is a good sign that the speaker knew the family well. what the second account fits the war in slavonia in 1945 is not a vague setting. it is one of the best-documented killing grounds of the european war's last months. the syrmian front ran from 21 october 1944 to 12 april 1945 across syrmia, slavonia and baranja. the yugoslav partisans lost more than 13,500 killed covering roughly 140 kilometres between belgrade and vinkovci over nearly six months of winter fighting. when the front broke on 12 april, the 1st and 3rd armies advanced west through slavonia . he had already seen the war close up. he was twenty when german aircraft destroyed about half of senj on 7-8 october 1943 , killing thirty of the town's residents - among them, on the second day, his uncle by marriage pavao kosina . a man born in 1923 was twenty-one or twenty-two in that campaign - precisely the cohort mobilised into it, much of it from newly-liberated croatia with minimal training. and an unknown grave is the ordinary outcome, not the strange one: thousands of those dead were buried where they fell. the detail that rings true. that the family cut his name into his grandparents' stone because there was no body is a specific, unglamorous, expensive act. people do it when someone does not come back from somewhere far away. it is much harder to explain if he died of a snakebite on the hill above the town. new evidence, september 2026 the grave says she was right about the grave a photograph of the blazevic plot at senj - recovered from the myheritage media library, where it had been sitting untouched - can be checked against nives blazevic's account line by line. it matches. ljubomir blazevic ✳1891 †1966 · milka blazevic rod. papic ✳1886 †1971 · oto blazevic ✳1923 †1945 · mario blazevic ✳1933 †1984 - and, on a later plaque, kata ✳1924 †2007 and leo ✳1920 †2008. she said "they put his name in … [the] grave" the stone oto blazevic ✳ 1923 † 1945 is cut into it, between his mother and his brother mario. she said "and now leo is there, and katica " the stone a separate, later, black plaque below reads leo ✳ 1920 † 2008 and kata ✳ 1924 † 2007 - katica. she said "his grandmother's and grandfather's grave" the stone the names are oto's parents . but nives blazevic was born in 1953 - ljubomir and milka were her grandparents. she is describing the grave from where she stands in the family, which is what people do. what this does and does not settle. it does not show that oto died in slavonia. it shows that the witness who said so knew this grave in exact detail , including two burials added more than sixty years after his death - and that the family commemorated him on a stone rather than at a grave of his own, which is what you do for a man who does not come back. the snakebite account now sits second. how this archive leaves it documented born 1923, senj. died 1945, with the death place entered in the tree as senj . son of ljubomir blazevic and milka papic; brother of leo, karmela, hedviga, ljubomir, mario and anton. family lore, first snakebite. attributed to ivan defranceski, who was there. family lore, second killed in the war in slavonia, no known grave, name added to his grandparents' plot. attributed to nives blazevic. corroborated nives's account, in its checkable parts: his name on the family stone, and leo and katica added to it later. the grave → contradiction still unresolved as to cause. the tree's own death place of senj agrees with neither account cleanly - it contradicts slavonia outright, and it is also exactly what a family would enter when the real place was unknown. what would settle it. the croatian state archives hold second world war military and civil death records, and the yugoslav war victims register ( popis zrtava rata ) is searchable by name and birth year. a single entry for oto blazevic, b. 1923, senj would end the question in either direction. nobody has yet looked. open questions → both accounts are kept because pretending otherwise is how family myths become family history - and because one of these two people was right. method →

q: papic porters, carriers and an innkeeper on the senj waterfront - and, one generation on, a woman supervising the floor of the senj and selce papic porters, carriers and an innkeeper on the senj waterfront - and, one generation on, a woman supervising the floor of the town's cigarette factory. 116 published people 1742 earliest birth year 4 distinct spellings in the tree one change in four documents the tree lists josip "joso" papic's occupations as trhonosa, bremenar, gostionicar - load-carrier, porter, innkeeper - as though they were three trades in a row. four parish registers give him four words, and only one of them is a change. at his own wedding in 1885 he is a bremenar ; at his daughter milka's baptism in 1886 , a trhonosa ; at his daughter anica's in 1888 , a tezak . those are not three trades - they are three words a priest reached for to mean a man who works with his body : burden-carrier, load-carrier, labourer. then at milka's wedding in 1907 he is a gostionicar . that is the change. he owns the inn. milka → the tobacco factory his daughter milka lucia papic (1886-1971) - hedviga's mother - was supervisor of workers at the cigarette factory in senj, an address the tree records as ul. stjepana radica 4 , "now a textile factory". she was baptised at senj on 19 october 1886 , ten days after her birth, with josip glavicic and ivka filipovic as godparents - one of the best-cited entries in this archive. a name changing in front of us the selce line is entered as "georgius juraj (joannis) papa 'jure' antic papic " - carrying antic and papic at once - and seventy-nine people in this tree are written papic (papa) . the register settles that this is a real alternation and not a transcriber's slip: in the 1885 marriage entry the groom is josip papic and his father, on the very same line, is juraj papa . and the doubling is old: the 1806 baptismal entry for josephum at vinodol enters his mother as "matre marthe antich papa " - both names on one line, eighty years before the tree's papic (papa) . his godfather is the village judge , judice mathia jellichich - of the family he would marry into. whether antic and papic were ever two families is now the open question. open questions → why the papici have no house number the blazevici can be traced through a single house number because the village registers of krmpote and krivi put record every child against one - smokvica 114 , krivi put 136 . the senj register does not. under mjesto obitavanja i kucni broj - place of residence and house number - the papic entries say simply "senj" , and nothing else. that is a difference between a town and a village, not between two families. it also means the zadruga that is visible at smokvica would be invisible here even if it existed , and no amount of reading senj baptisms will show it. the other half of this family hedviga's descent is not all peasants, and the other half arrives through this family. josip papic's mother was matija pilipic , and through her the line runs into karlobag , a free royal city on the coast under the velebit, and the register there speaks a different language about them: dominus at the 1768 baptism of josephus pilipic; negotiator - merchant - when he is named as deceased in 1838; and godparents who are franciscus de justiniani , a venetian patrician name, and, in 1777, pro-colonel joannes hallinich de zirfeld with the wife of centurion daniel de kalbenaeck . a colonel and a captain's wife stood for an uroda child; a giustiniani for a pilipic. that is not the world of smokvica 114 , and the two meet in one woman four generations later. the marriage, 3 february 1885 senj marriages p.192, entry 5. josip papic , bremenar , of senj, aged 27 , bachelor, married antonia perpic of krivi put , resident at senj, aged 26 , spinster. banns published; married by the chaplain mirko babic . his parents: juraj papa, tezak - a farm labourer - and matia rod. pilipic . hers: ivan perpic, seljak - peasant - and luca rod. perpic , which supplies a maiden name the tree did not carry: antonija's mother was herself a perpic . the witnesses are franjo and toma perpic , both peasants - the bride's q: photograph these seven places and four kinds of paper. each one is here because a specific claim on this site would move if somebody stoo for whoever is next in croatia photograph these seven places and four kinds of paper. each one is here because a specific claim on this site would move if somebody stood in front of it with a phone - not because it would be nice to have. this archive has been built from a family tree, a media library and about thirty pages of parish register read on a screen. nobody involved in it has stood in any of these places. a phone is enough for all of it; none of this needs an appointment, and most of it needs no permission. photograph the whole thing and then the detail. a stone shot only close up cannot be placed in its row; a stone shot only wide cannot be read. and photograph the ones that look like nothing - a wrong house number is worth knowing too. go here first senj - the cemetery at sv. vid the blazevic grave: ljubomir 1892-1966, milka 1886-1971, oto 1923-1945, mario 1933-1984. photograph the whole stone and each line close. tereza zubrinic's stone, 1867-1931, restored by the kosina family in 1991, with the wooden cross for vlc. antun kosina 1921-2003 standing against it. pavao and anka kosina's grave - his stone reads nevina zrtva zracnog napadaja na senj, an innocent victim of the air raid. toma blazevic was buried here on 28 july 1907 and stanko papic on 4 june 1903. neither grave has been looked for. a cemetery register or a surviving stone would place them. smokvica krmpotska - house 114 the house itself, if it still stands, and the number if it is still on it. the neighbouring numbers, 112 and 116, so the run can be placed on the ground. anything carved or dated on the building. six documented years - 1838, 1882, 1884, 1888, 1890, 1895 - hold toma's children, pavao's children, jurko's children and two different men called ivo blazevic. it is the zadruga the whole of question 1b turns on, and nobody in this archive has seen it. klenovica and povile - house 22 the house, if it stands, and the number on it - in both villages, because they may be the same building. whether klenovica 22 and povile 22 are one house, two houses, or one house the registers gave two village names. the kalanj graves in the klenovica cemetery beyond the one already photographed (lovro 1906-1965, ana 1919-1971, ivan 1942-1996, marijan 1944-2009). sixty-seven published people are entered at house 22 between 1840 and 1890 - the largest single household in this archive, ahead of smokvica 114 and krivi put 136. eleven couples have children recorded under both village names, which is why it is thought to be one house. nobody has stood in front of it. krivi put - house 136 the house, and 113 and 129 if the numbers survive. the church of the parish, and any war memorial. antonija perpic was born at 136 in 1859 into a household the register calls confiniarii. three prpic house numbers are known and none has been seen. when you are passing crikvenica - the hotel therapia the building, now the kvarner palace - the facade and, if they will let you in, the room that was the dining hall. any historic photograph the hotel keeps of its own interwar years. hedviga is remembered singing here. it is the only thing anyone has ever said about what she did, and the building is still standing - bought in 2013 and renamed. a photograph would turn a sentence of lore into something you can look at. senj - the tobacco factory the building on ul. stjepana radica 4, now a textile works. any plaque, date stone or surviving signage. milka supervised women rolling cigarettes here and antonija blazevic held the same grade. across ten register pages between 1909 and 1919, most young women marrying in senj worked in it. if you get that far otocac and sumecica sumecica house 24, if the numbering survives. the parish church at otocac. prozor houses 50 and 245. the 1834 baptism puts a confiniarius household at sumecica 24. the zubrinici held five frontier offices out of these villages. karlobag the parish church. anything marking the town as a free royal city - the registers call it hujus civitatis. four generations of pilipici, urodas, smojvers and gerkacs, with a giustiniani standing godfather and a baron von holstein on the same page. the most socially distinct part of this descent. and anything on paper what why it matters here anything written on the back of a photograph studio stamps date and place a picture better than anything else here. fifteen photographs on /faces have no caption but a camera filename. letters, in any language nothing in this archive is in the family's own words. not one letter. identity papers, passports, work books a yugoslav passport application would date the emigration that question 1f cannot. funeral cards and death notices they carry the date, the parish and often the surviving relatives, all three. if you are holding a photograph and cannot say who is in it, that is worth as much - the contact sheet is fifteen pictures this archive cannot vouch for, and one conversation would close most of it.

it is where a whole family came from. senj the port town. birthplace of hedviga, milka and josip papic; deathplace of toma blazevic, ljubomir, milka and antonija. everything converges here. smokvica krmpotska the blazevic village in the vinodol hills, settled by bunjevci in the 17th century. house 114 is toma's. krivi put the prpic village on the senj mountain. house 136 produced 35 people in this tree. otocac the zubrinic town, in the gacka valley in lika, inland across the velebit. selce on the vinodol coast - the antic-papic and jellicic lines. karlobag south down the coast under the velebit - the pilipic, uroda, smojver and gerkacs lines, and the archive's deepest generation. klenovica & povile the kalanj villages, on the coast between novi vinodolski and senj - and, it turns out, not where the kalanji are from. house 22 is one house under two village names, and holds 67 people. brinje inland, over the kapela, and the only place on this list nobody has ever searched. the kalanj baptism of 1864 calls the parents brinjensis parochiae ruricolae - country people of the parish of brinje. kalanj, perkovic and boric all appear there. prozor & sumecica the two otocac villages the oldest zubrinic entries name - prozor 46 and 50, sumecica 2 and 24. six people left prozor for new york between 1907 and 1912. port pirie south australia. the zubrinic emigration of about 1884, and the zubrinich spelling. every place, counted every place is a link: it opens the register filtered to the people recorded there. births and deaths of published people carrying one of the eight senj for a lead-smelting town on the far side of the world, and his name changed on arrival. twenty of his descendants are in this tree, and every one of them is a zubrinich. the first of them is joannes / juan / ivan / ive / john zubrinic - a man carried in this tree under five versions of one given name - born 1860 and died 1930 at port pirie, south australia . his eldest recorded child is born there in 1885 , which puts his arrival at about 1884 . from that child onward the surname in the register is zubrinich . not once does it revert. the names → why port pirie port pirie is not a random landfall. smelting began there in 1889 , and it grew into one of the largest lead smelters in the world - heavy, dangerous, continuous work that paid, and that hired men without english. croatians began arriving in south australia from the dalmatian islands in the 1890s , and many of them went to port pirie and broken hill . further groups came with the economic depression in dalmatia and medimurje between 1910 and 1913 , and again after the political unrest of 1922 . the family's later moves confirm the pattern exactly: this tree records zubrinich deaths at broken hill and whyalla - the silver-lead mine and the steelworks. they followed the metal. an anomaly worth flagging. ivan's birthplace is entered as "senj, split-dalmatia, croatia" . senj is in lika-senj county, not split-dalmatia; this is an automated place-match error, and it matters because it is the kind of thing that later gets read as evidence of dalmatian origin. open questions → the australian records in they were simply never looked for, because one spelling was searched and the other was not. the other emigration → added 13 september 2026 nor only to south australia every one of the 24 australians above is in south australia or, later, at broken hill . that is the whole australian story this archive has told. queensland's own historical index was searched for the first time on 13 september 2026, and it holds one zubrinich. stanley joseph zubrinich married joanna marian josephine clowes in queensland on 15 november 1947 - registration 1947/b/15067 . he is not in this tree, and no stanley joseph is. a candidate, not a relative. nothing here shows how he joins. but two things make him worth the next hour somebody spends. the surname is vanishingly rare , and the anglicised -ich ending is the specific spelling this family adopted on arrival at port pirie and never once reverted from - so a zubrinich in australia is far more likely to be one of these than to be a separate landing. and the given name is the family's: a stanley was born at port pirie in 1896 and died there in 1897, and these are people who re-used the names of children they lost. a stanley joseph marrying in 1947 would have been born around the 1920s, which is exactly the generation of terrence joseph (1924) and maurice william (1922). his marriage certificate would name his parents and settle it. the nulls are worth recording with it. queensland's register covers births to 1926, marriages to 1951 and deaths to 1996, and across that span it holds no zubrinic , no blazevic and no subrinich . the three blazevich entries are a queensland household of thomas bogin blazevich, who married jane chambers in 1940, and are unconnected to anyone here. added 14 september 2026 · find a grave the graves, and who lies in them together this archive had never used a cemetery index. find a grave holds 72 zubrinich memorials and not one of them is in croatia - twenty-nine at port pirie , thirteen at enfield in adelaide, six at timmins in ontario , four at whyalla , two at broken hill , two in pennsylvania , one in california . the whole of this surname's recorded burial is emigration. sixteen of the 72 are people on this site. the other 56 are not, and the plot numbers say who they were: a lot number is a household claim , and it is one a parish register cannot make. rose has dates. john zubrinich lies in cc, lot 26 at port pirie, and beside him in grave 2 is rose zubrinich, 17 march 1860 -
