q: rhodes hedviga's second husband was born on rhodes in 1913, into a sephardic community that was almost entirely destroyed in 19 santou isaac codron, 1913-1997 rhodes hedviga's second husband was born on rhodes in 1913, into a sephardic community that was almost entirely destroyed in 1944 - and he died in south africa in 1997. how he came to be alive to marry her is the most interesting unanswered question in this archive. the tree records him plainly and briefly: santou (shemtov) isaac codron , born 13 september 1913 at rhodes , died 16 april 1997 in south africa of cardio-respiratory arrest, married to hedviga about 1973 . that is every fact held on him. each one opens onto a large history. shemtov - shem tov , "good name" - is a sephardic given name, and codron is a known rhodes jewish surname. he was, on the face of the record, a rhodesli . 23 july 1944 what happened to the community he was born into rhodes held a sephardic jewish community that had been there since the fifteenth century, speaking judeo-spanish - the language their ancestors carried out of spain in 1492. in the quarter called la djuderia it was still, in 1944, a living world. on 20 july 1944 the ss ordered the island's jews to assemble for a document check. 1,615 people from rhodes , together with 94 from kos , were packed into the cargo holds of livestock ships, taken to the greek mainland, and put on a train. they arrived at auschwitz on 16 august 1944 after what is generally called the longest deportation journey of the holocaust . about 1,200 were murdered on arrival. roughly 150 survived. santou codron was thirty in july 1944. if he was on rhodes that month, he was almost certainly on that transport - and the odds of walking out of it were about one in eleven. the likelier explanation, and why he probably was not there - because the rhodes jews had been leaving for southern africa for fifty years, and that is exactly where he turns up. rhodesli men began going to africa for work at the end of the nineteenth century; mousa and solomon benatar settled in southern rhodesia in 1895 . emigration accelerated through the 1920s and 1930s, to the belgian congo , southern rhodesia and south africa - for economic reasons first, and from 1938 because of the italian racial laws, rhodes then being italian territory. sephardim from rhodes settled in salisbury , today's harare, and founded a synagogue there in 1932 . in all, close to two thousand jews from rhodes lived in the congo and southern rhodesia between the 1920s and the 1960s. now set hedviga's own movements beside that. she came to south africa from zimbabwe - that is, from rhodesia - in april 1975 , and she is recorded as marrying codron around 1973 , which places the marriage in the rhodesian years. so the meeting has an obvious setting. a croatian woman from senj and a sephardic jew from rhodes, both a long way from home, in the small european society of late-colonial rhodesia - a community he most likely belonged to because his family had been part of that specific migration for decades before the war. this is an inference, not a document. added 14 september 2026 · find a grave the question this page asked itself, answered - and it is not a comfortable answer the table below has said since it was written that who among the codrons was deported in july 1944 has not been checked here . it has now been checked - not against yad vashem, which remains the right register, but against the index of gravestones. it took an afternoon and it should have been done long ago. fourteen codron memorials at auschwitz. eight of them share one date. that date is 16 august 1944 - the day this page already names as the arrival of the rhodes transport, after the longest deportation journey of the holocaust. born name died 1873 caden hasson codron 16 aug 1944 20 nov 1873 ruben bension codron 16 aug 1944 3 aug 1900 leone codron 16 aug 1944 21 mar 1902 hitzkia codron 16 aug 1944 20 jan 1906 nissim codron 1944 21 dec 1906 clara simsolo codron 1944 11 feb 1907 amelia hasson codron 16 aug 1944 9 dec 1911 regina capelluto codron 16 aug 1944 20 apr 1925 maurizio mose codron 1944 11 apr 1927 lina codron 1944 26 jun 1928 maria codron 1944 1 sep 1929 elsa codron - fourteen 1944 24 jul 1933 alessandro codron - eleven 16 aug 1944 28 apr 1939 rachele codron - five 16 aug 1944 the married surnames carried into the family are hasson , simsolo and capelluto - all of them rhodes sephardic names. santou codron was thirty-one when this happened, and he was alive in 1997 to be buried in south africa. the cemetery on the island - 1768 to 1937 the same index holds about twenty codron graves in the jewish cemetery of the island of rhodes , with the row numbers, running from 1768 to 1937 - that is, from before the american revolution to seven years before the community was destroyed. yaacov codron, 1768 is the earliest. then sara de salomon-jeuda (1871), david de abraham (1878), dona de joseph-franco (1892), rica de haim (1892), rosa de abraham (1899), lunar de hizkia (1901), raffael (1902), isaac de joseph and miriam de nissim (1904), rebecca mujer de samuel-israel (1910), isaac de abraham (1918), risula and samuel de matalbria (1920), abraham de nissim (1923), behora simha david (1926), paligoria de behor-menasce and rachel de reuben (1932), risula de isaac (1937), and caden de abraham signoru franco codron, 1852-1941 . look at how they are named. de abraham , de nissim , de joseph , de haim , de reuben - son or daughter of . mujer de - wife of. this archive has spent weeks on the croatian equivalent: «georgius jellicich, antonii » in the selce death register, the patronymic that distinguishes one man of a common name from another. two communities that never met, a thousand miles apart, solving the same problem the same way. and a codron family in cape town six codrons lie in the pinelands jewish cemeteries at cape town - which is the other end of the migration this page argues he took. died name cemetery 17 jun 1972 leon codron pinelands 1 26 may 1974 jack codron pinelands 1 13 jun 1985 albert codron pinelands 2 15 mar 1989 raie codron pinelands 2 14 oct 1997 guditha codron pinelands 2 16 aug 2000 isaac nissim codron pinelands 2 two of those are worth staring at. guditha codron died on 14 october 1997 - six months after santou , in the same country. and isaac nissim codron carries both of the names that surround him: santou's own full name is santou isaac codron , and nissim is a codron name on rhodes three times over in the list above. codrons also appear at the stockholm jewish memorial - a survivors' memorial - at the melbourne chevra kadisha , and at home of peace memorial park in los angeles , one of them in a plot marked western jewish institute . rhodes, auschwitz, cape town, stockholm, melbourne, los angeles: the shape of what happened to one island's families. none of this is joined to santou by a document. it is the same surname, the same island and the same community, and that is all it is. what it does is answer the question this page has been asking itself: the codrons of rhodes were deported, and fourteen of them are memorialised at auschwitz. whether he lost his own parents and brothers and sisters there, or whether his branch had left for africa in the 1920s as this page argues, is still not known - and the two possibilities are no longer equally comfortable. the auschwitz entries are memorials, not graves , and the index is compiled by volunteers, not an archive. the search register → what this archive does and does not claim documented born 13 september 1913, rhodes. died 16 april 1997, south africa, of cardio-respiratory arrest. married hedviga blazevic c. 1973. inferred that he was a rhodes sephardi - from the given name shemtov , the surname codron and the birthplace together. inferred that he most likely reached southern africa before the war, as part of the documented rhodes-to-rhodesia migration - because he was alive in 1973 and because that route was well travelled. not claimed that he survived auschwitz. nothing in this record says he was deported, and treating him as a survivor because he was born in the right place at the right time would be an invention. it would also be a serious one. not claimed that his family escaped - or that it did not. checked, 14 september 2026: fourteen codrons are memorialised at auschwitz and eight of them share the date 16 august 1944. not one of them is yet joined to him by a document. yad vashem and the rhodes jewish museum registers remain the place to settle it. what would settle it. south african immigration and naturalisation papers would give his arrival year and last residence outright. the rhodes jewish museum and yad vashem hold community and deportation registers in which a codron born 13 september 1913 would either appear or be absent - and either answer is worth having.

a port that the railway killed in 1873 . it is also a war story, and the war reached the family directly. nothing in the family tree says so ; the dates do. what happened italy capitulated on 8 september 1943 , and the italian occupation zone along the adriatic collapsed. senj, with its harbour and its road up to lika, became one of the most important partisan ports on the coast: weapons and war material were concentrated in the town and ships lay in the harbour. on 7 and 8 october 1943 german aircraft bombed the town and the port. 52 killed - 30 local residents and 22 foreigners ~60 civilians recorded seriously or lightly wounded 50% of the town destroyed to its foundations; only about a quarter of buildings still habitable figures from the croatian scholarly literature on the german bombing of senj in 1943. sources → the family in it anka blazevic's household anka blazevic (1893-1953) was ljubomir's sister - hedviga's aunt, and the radnica who worked the floor of the tobacco factory alongside her sister-in-law milka . on 20 november 1919 she married pavao kosina , born at senj on 15 march 1894. pavao kosina b. 15 march 1894, senj - died 8 october 1943 , the second day of the bombing otilija kosina b. 1920 - died 11 november 1943 , five weeks after her father, and her stone does not call her a victim of anything . she was cin. velike zupe , a clerk of the wartime region. this page said «no day recorded» until the family's own gravestone was read on 21 september 2026. antun kosina b. 1921 - died 2003. a priest : his cross reads vlc. , velecasni . he founded the croatian catholic mission at ludwigshafen in 1967 and led it until 1985 - twenty-two when his father was killed, and forty years later the head of a mission of four thousand. his life → oskar kosina b. 4 september 1922, senj - died 15 january 1954, buenos aires , aged thirty-one. his printed memorial card gives the day - and reads ✻ 4. iv. 1922 against the tree's 4 september. recorded, not resolved. he landed at buenos aires on 9 october 1947 off the philippa , already married. neda kosina b. 1924 - died 7 september 1943 , a month before the raid. her stone calls her maturantica , a school-leaver, and zrtva zracnog napada - a victim of an air attack . so senj was bombed more than once that autumn. krizan kosina b. 1940 - died 1941, an infant anka outlived them by a decade and died in 1953. confirmed, september 2026 - an inference becomes a document the stone says it outright this page first said pavao kosina was probably one of the thirty, and was careful to add that the date came from the family tree rather than from any record. then his grave was found in the media library. the kosina plot, senj. three portrait medallions below the inscription. ovdje pociva u miru bozjem pavao kosina ✳ 15.iii.1894. · pog. 8.x.1943. nevina zrtva zracnog napadaja na senj u znak sjecanja podize - zahvalna supruga i sinovi "here rests in god's peace pavao kosina, born 15 march 1894, killed 8 october 1943. an innocent victim of the air raid on senj. raised in memory by his grateful wife and sons." pog. is poginuo - killed, the word used for a violent death rather than an ordinary one. the family did not merely record the date; they recorded the cause, and their judgement of it . nevina zrtva - an innocent victim. and one word carries the rest of the story. the stone was raised by supruga i sinovi - his wife and his sons . not his daughters. otilija and neda were both dead by the end of that same year. the plate below also carries krizan (1940-1941), the infant, and anka herself, who outlived them all to 1953. where the kosinas came from a marriage in a front room, 1857 and behind that, carniola. pavao's father martin kozina was born at zgornje bitnje near kranj, in what is now slovenia, on 16 november 1841 - illegitimate, to gertraud kosina , in her brother's house. the line is now traced to his grandparents, franz kosinar and maria «mina» dortschen, who married on 27 october 1800. the kosina → pavao kosina's mother was angelika boras (1857-1902), and the boras reach this archive through her. their own beginning is one of the more human entries in it. senj marriages, 9 february 1857 , entry 52 - caelebs josephus boras , filius denatorum josephi et annae boras natae butvalz - cum vidua maria … in domo privata copulate fuere. ages 32 and 28. they married in a private house , by dispensation of the bishop - a departure from the parish church that usually means illness, urgency or irregularity. he is entered as a bachelor , she as a widow . and they already had three children : ana and anton in 1854, ivan in 1855. angelika follows the marriage , later in 1857. it is a legitimation - a union of some years put right in a front room under episcopal licence. her brother ivan boras (1855-1926) went into the carinska sluzba , the customs service , a state post in a port town; her grandmother's name was anna butvalz , german, as ana untersinger is in the zubrinic line. two german surnames marry into this family in the frontier century, which is what an imperial administration leaves behind. angelika died in 1902 . she did not see her son marry anka blazevic in 1919, and she did not see 1943. what is claimed, and what is not documented german aircraft bombed senj on 7-8 october 1943 , killing 30 local residents and 22 others and destroying about half the town. documented in the tree pavao kosina died on 8 october 1943 . documented that he was one of them - the stone says so. see below. not claimed that otilija (1943, undated) or neda ( 7 september 1943) died in the bombing. neda's date is a month before it - and the day before italy's capitulation. three deaths in one household in one year is not one event until something says it is. what would settle it. the senj death register for 1943 , which would give cause and place for all three; and the published list of the town's bombing victims, which exists in the local historical literature. open questions → where it leaves the rest of the family hedviga was seventeen she was born in senj in 1926 and her children were born there and at crikvenica in 1948, 1951 and 1953 - so she was in the town, or near it, when half of it came down. her brother oto was twenty, and had two years to live . the first version of her page here said she was "fifteen when the war reached the coast". it reached her street. and then argentina her cousin oskar kosina (1922-1954) landed at buenos aires on 9 october 1947 , off the philippa out of genoa and already married, and died there on 15 january 1954 aged thirty-one. that is the second documented destination of this family after port pirie - and it matches the surname statistics exactly: of the sixty-nine people in the world spelling the name zubrinic , twenty-nine are in argentina , the largest group anywhere. the names → 

s: Senj made this family and then stopped being able to feed it. Every occupation in the record — day labourer, porter, sai
q: senj senj made this family and then stopped being able to feed it. every occupation in the record - day labourer, porter, sai the town the railway went around senj senj made this family and then stopped being able to feed it. every occupation in the record - day labourer, porter, sailor, cigarette-factory hand - is a consequence of one decision taken in 1873. senj sits under the velebit at the head of the senjska draga , where the bura comes off the mountain hard enough to stop traffic. it is one of the oldest towns on the croatian coast, and for four hundred years it was a place of consequence: a free royal town, a bishopric, a habsburg military port, and the home of the uskoks . 1537-1618 the uskoks and nehaj when the ottomans took klis in 1537, its defenders - refugees the slavs called uskoci , "the ones who jumped in" - fell back to senj. the habsburgs put them on the frontier payroll and let them raid. they became, depending on who was writing, a christian bulwark or a pirate confederacy; in practice both, because vienna paid them irregularly and they took the difference out of venetian and ottoman shipping. in 1558 the captain ivan lenkovic built nehaj on the hill above the town, using stone from the churches and monasteries outside the walls so that a besieger would have nothing to shelter behind. it was the uskok headquarters until the uskok war of 1615-18 ended with venice and vienna agreeing to disperse them inland. nehaj still stands over the town, and it is the thing everyone photographs. this archive claims no uskok descent. the uskoks were broken up in 1618 and the earliest person in this tree is born about 1717 - a century later. what the uskok period explains is not the family's blood but the family's place : it is why there was a fortified, garrisoned, habsburg-administered town here at all, and why the empty mountain behind it was about to be settled on purpose. the settlement → the turning point 1873: the railway goes to rijeka senj's whole nineteenth century was built on being the port where the lika highlands met the sea. timber, wool and livestock came down the roads from the interior and went out through senj. then the karlovac-rijeka railway opened in 1873 and did not come here. the traffic followed the rails to rijeka. senj's port trade collapsed, and it never recovered. this is the single most important economic fact in this archive, because the family's recorded work sits directly downstream of it: toma blazevic 1838-1907 nadnicar - day labourer. born at br. 114, smokvica krmpotska ; died at senj and buried there. a man who came off the mountain to a town that had no work left. josip "joso" papic 1857-1939 trhonosa, bremenar, gostionicar - load-carrier, porter, innkeeper. the first two are the same job twice: carrying other people's goods on your back for a fee. the third is what he made of it. ljubomir blazevic 1892-1966 mornar - sailor. born at rijeka , not senj - the family had already followed the work to the port that got the railway. he came back, and died at senj. milka papic 1886-1971 supervisor of workers at the cigarette factory , tvornica duhana , senj. her sister-in-law anka blazevic (1893-1953) was a radnica - a floor worker - at the same factory. a town of incomers, and the register says where from page 107 of the senj baptisms holds eight entries from 1885. four of them - half - record not a mother's trade but the parish she came from . katarina roncevic of jablanac , down the coast katarina stimac of the parish of crnoluska roza babic of the parish of starigrad tonka papic rodj. prpic iz krivogputa - from krivi put this archive already knows antonija prpic is of krivi put, because her 1859 baptism is there. here the senj register says it too - twenty-six years later and a mountain away, a town clerk recording that this woman is not from the town. so the family's arrival in senj was not unusual. it was what senj was. the blazevici coming down from smokvica and the papici from selce are not exceptions to a settled population - they are the population, and the book was recording it in half its entries. the same page gives the fathers' trades: nadcestar (road overseer), bremenar (porter), tezak (labourer), mornar (sailor), with trgovac and postolar among the godparents. what they did → the tobacco factory the habsburg tobacco monopoly was extended to croatia, slavonia and the military frontier by an imperial patent of 20 november 1850 , effective from march 1851, and state tobacco factories followed across the region. senj's was one of them, and for two generations of this family it was the employer of last resort in a town with no port trade - women's work, indoors, waged, and steady in a way that carrying sacks was not. after the second world war the senj factory was liquidated and its cigarette-making machinery was transferred to the tobacco factory at rovinj . the tree records the building's later life exactly: the address is given as ul. stjepana radica 4, 53270 senj , with the note that it "now is a textile factory". and it is why these families met. one page of the senj marriage register for 1918 carries three brides entered as radnica u tvornici duhana - from otocac/sumecica , from krivi put , and from senj . those are the three places this archive comes from. counting milka , her sister-in-law anka , antonija blazevic and ana papic , six women of these families worked that floor. the factory was the institution that brought the mountain villages into the town - and it is a large part of why a blazevic of smokvica, a prpic of krivi put and a zubrinic of otocac end up in one family. unverified here. the senj factory's founding date, size and closure year have not been confirmed from a croatian source by this archive. the monopoly patent and the transfer of machinery to rovinj are documented generally; the specific history of the senj plant is an open question . two days that finished what the railway started 7-8 october 1943 after italy's capitulation senj became one of the most important partisan ports on the adriatic, and german aircraft bombed the town and harbour over two days in october 1943. thirty local residents were killed and about half the town was destroyed to its foundations ; only a quarter of the buildings were still habitable. hedviga was seventeen. her aunt's husband died on the second day. senj, 1943 → and then the boats out a port town with no port sends its people away. this tree records the destinations plainly: port pirie in south australia , where ivan zubrinic went about 1884 and where his descendants still are; buenos aires , where hedviga's cousin oskar kosina landed off the philippa on 9 october 1947 and died on 15 january 1954 ; and then, two generations later, africa - hedviga to rhodesia and then to johannesburg in april 1975 . september 2026 - the by-name becomes the surname, in two documents this archive has argued for years that papa is a nadimak attached to antic . two senj entries, twenty-eight years apart, show it stop being one. 1 november 1857 - the baptism of ahnentafel 6, in the prose register: anno domini 1857 die 1 nbris. ego joannes tusic , cooperator loci, baptizavi josephum , filium legitimum, romano-catholicum, joannis papa et ejus uxoris mathiae pilipic . levantibus patrinis … ✝ michael stipancic . the date matches the tree to the day, the parents are named, and the godfather signs with a cross . 3 may 1885 - the same man's marriage, entry 5: josip papic, bremenar , of senj, aged 27 - son of «juraj papa, tezak, i matia rodjena pilipic» read them together. the father is joannis papa in 1857 and juraj papa in 1885 - and never antic in either . the son is already papic . the by-name has displaced the surname outright in the parish register by 1857 and hardened into a new surname within one generation , and both halves of that are now documents rather than an argument. the by-names → the marriage also names ahnentafel 7's parents - ivan perpic and luce - which settles ahnentafel 14 and gives 15 her given name from a register.

peninsula, eighty miles west of senj, and nowhere near the velebit littoral where every other family on this site lives. the remaining record is on pag . no marriage joins them to anyone here not one sestan marries into any of the other eight families. their marriages go to defranceschi - three of them - and then to depras, androsic, krismanic and gasparic. defranceschi is hedviga's husband's family, not hers. the path, in full the shortest route from hedviga to the nearest sestan is eleven steps : out through ivan defranceski to his father ante, to josip de franceschi, to antonius, to giovanni battista, to teresa grach , to an unnamed spouse, and then across a node entered in the tree as grah's for investigation (not real) , to gologorica grah , to josephus grah, to rosa sestan . remove that one node and there is no path at all. every one of the fifty-five becomes unreachable. they are published here because somebody was investigating whether they belonged, and the investigation is still sitting in the tree in the place where a father should be. labels where the father should be → what this archive is doing about it keeping them, and marking every one. the method here is to report the tree rather than edit it, and these are real records of real people at gologorica between 1780 and 1947 - the doubt is about the join , not about them. deleting fifty-five people to make a statistic look better would be the opposite of what this archive is for. so all fifty-five now carry a notice at the head of their own page saying that every route from hedviga to them passes through a sorting label. a reader should not meet these names on a site about a woman from senj without being told what connects them to her - and equally should not be told they are a parent, a spouse, a child - with no page and no slug . this is the fifth tool in this archive found blind to the unpublished, and the second time on this very evidence. «ivan defranceski 1925-1995» was photographed at senj and filed as a surname that does not occur once in this tree. he is hedviga's husband . he now matches his own gravestone because the matcher was taught where to look, not because somebody wrote a correction by hand. searching the published people is not searching the tree. five more names came back with him - three spalj, a sojat - all of them people this tree carries and this site has never published. and then it happened a sixth time, 20 september 2026, to the one file written to prevent it. sources/found.psv exists for a single reason: a person who is in a register and not in the tree had nowhere to be recorded. so it holds the one population a stone is most likely to name and the tree least likely to explain - and the matcher could not see it either. the cost was one name, and it is the name that proves the point. «matilda papic 1895-1921» stands third on a senj cross. she was photographed, read at full resolution, found to be absent from the tree, and written down in found.psv as a discovery - they may well be right, and none of them has been tested. 31 branches simply end. nothing is hidden for space. where the chart stops, the archive stops, and how far back sets out what each of those endings would take to get past. not every wall is the same kind of wall the list under the chart used to say the same sentence about all 31 of them - no parents are recorded, and where the line goes next is not known. that is true of all of them and useful about none of them, because they are not one thing. 11 of the 31 are name problems, not research problems. seven are women the tree gives a given name and no surname at all; two more wear their husband's surname, which is the tree's convention and not a record of what they were born; two are a bare surname with no given name, which asserts only what the child's own name already says. there is nothing to search for until a marriage entry or a child's baptism supplies the missing half. more have no place recorded anywhere on the line - and neither will a searcher who only types one of them. this page exists because the archive was caught not doing it. on 17 september 2026 somebody asked whether the research searches all the variations of a name. for surnames it does, and it has been proved: zubrinich returns 191 records, zubrinic a different 119, zubrinick ten more - one family. for given names it did not. the emigration target list handed the searcher whatever form the family tree happened to hold, which in these parishes is usually the latin of the baptismal entry. tested against the index the same hour: firstname=josip returns records firstname=joseph returns records firstname=josephus 0 firstname=giuseppe 0 and the index's own «include name variants» box is on by default and still returns nothing for josephus , so whatever it expands, it does not expand across the languages a croatian parish was written in. where the searching is recorded → a name you have looked up is a link you can send. the address bar follows the search - ?n=mihovil - so a card can go to a cousin or an archivist and open on exactly what you were looking at. two kinds of cell. a form printed plainly is one this archive has actually met in one of its own records. a form marked like this ° is a lookup aid - the correct form in that language and the right thing to type into a hungarian or german index tomorrow, but not something written down here yet. 174 of the 343 forms below are attested - 51%. nothing decides that by hand: tools/names.py reads it out of the records, and the build refuses if a form the records contain is missing from the table. the first time that gate ran it found two men called mathaeus filed apart from the twenty-one matijas they belong to, separated by a single t . type a given name mihovil josephus zuane mathaeus jurko katalin gregorium joso frank mihaly copy link 40 names · 343 forms · 174 met in these records, 169 as lookup aids. the hole this page was built over the table was built from the men every name group here that has a latin feminine - joanna, josepha, georgia, jacoba, paulina - had nowhere to put her until 17 september 2026. eight joannas, two josephas, two georgias and a jacoba fell out of the fold entirely , and so out of every variant list built from it. that is the worst possible place for a hole. the women of this tree are already its weakest part - seven direct ancestors carry no surname at all, because a woman was entered under her husband's - and the one tool that would have helped somebody find them had been built from the men. five feminine groups were added and the fold now holds 40 names. the column no other archive here has latin is one language with six endings michaelem is not another form of the name. it is michael in the accusative, because the priest wrote baptizavi michaelem - «i baptised michael». nobody was ever called it, and nobody was ever indexed under it. and the sex is counted, not asserted. the fold declares matija a man's name. eight of the forty people written that way here are women - one of them ahnentafel 13, matia pilipic , whose marriage is row 4 of the work list . croatian matija is unisex and the table had one column for it, so this page counts the bearers instead. this matters more than it sounds. the family tree is built from what the register says, so the register's grammar walks straight into it: ten people in the emigration target list are named in an oblique case - gregorium, conradum, joannem, helenam, georgium, mathiam, elisabetham, joannam - and a search for any of them returns nothing for ever. tools/latin_cases.py already knew this about 47 people in this archive; what was missing was anything that used it before typing a name into a search box. the names, counted →

q: the zubrinic fragments this archive has said for months that joining the zubrinici is the largest piece of work left in it. counting it properl 422 records, 397 real people, 115 loose ends the zubrinic fragments this archive has said for months that joining the zubrinici is the largest piece of work left in it. counting it properly says something worse and more useful: 81 of the 115 loose ends are bare names with neither a date nor a place, and exactly one pair can be joined from what the tree holds. corrected: two numbers this archive published were both wrong the site has been saying "232 records resolving into 94 separate root ancestors" . neither figure survives checking. 232 was too low. the surname fold split on a bracket but not on a slash, so zubrinic / xubrinich and zubrinic zubrinic xubrinich - one surname written several ways in one field - never matched the surname list at all. the real figure is 422 . fixing it brought 214 people into this archive who had been sitting outside it, among them elias ilija zubrinic and casparus zubrinic - the subjects of two of this archive's own open questions . 94 was the right shape for the wrong reason. the true count is 115 , and it is high because of something the old number never named - see below. ninety-two people hang off an alphabet the tree contains 18 nodes whose entire given name is a single letter - m , j , t - each with a parent called "zubrinic zubrinix xubrinic zub" , and each holding as children the zubrinici whose names begin with that letter. one of them has 26 children ; another has 17. that is a filing system, not a family. between them these eighteen nodes hold 92 people . counted as parentage - which is what a naive read does - the zubrinici look joined. they are not: those 92 people are attached to the letter their name starts with and to nothing else. this archive's own sorting-bucket filter did not catch them, because a bucket is normally detected by words like "to be sorted" and these are named a through w . what is actually left, and what can be done with it state how many what it means anchored 7 a year and a place. these are the only ones a register search can start from. dated 26 a year and no place. searchable only if you already know the parish. placed 1 a place and no year. a century of register to read. bare 81 neither. a name and a surname. nothing in this archive will ever move them, and no amount of work on the tree will either. so the honest answer to "can the zubrinici be joined?" is no - not from here. 81 of 115 have nothing to search on. the joining has to come out of the otocac registers , and this archive has read two pages of them. the 4 pairs the tree can offer gregorius gregory zubrinic zubrinic xubrinich 1785 antonius zubrinic zubrinic xubrinich 1796 same village, born within a dozen years - working . these are not people. they are labels somebody typed into the father's slot while sorting, and this archive already found four of them being published as ancestors and removed them - from the list of people . nobody removed them from the list of parents . so a zubrinic whose only father is the phrase "brothers of josephus" was counted by this page as joined . across the whole archive, 21 sorting buckets are still acting as a parent , 218 published people hang off one , and 74 have no other parent at all - sumecica 2 . three alphabets, one name - and here is the proof the family is written xubrinich in the venetian-italian convention where x spelled the sound z ; zubrinich in the german-latin administrative hand; and zubrinic in modern croatian after gaj's reform. that was an argument until the otocac register was read. in the baptismal entry of 24 january 1834 the priest writes the father's name and underlines it : michael xubrinich . how to search it → they were frontier soldiers the same entry, kept in latin, gives the household's conditio in one word: confiniarius - a man of the military frontier , the militarised border the habsburgs ran against the ottomans, in which every household owed service. it places them ex pago shumechia n° 24 - the village of sumecica , house 24, outside otocac, itself a frontier regimental seat. the godparents say it twice over. the godfather is petrus, son of francis xubrinich , entered as vigiliarum ma[gister] - master of the watch - and pensioned . the godmother is maria, wife of joannes xubrinich, silvarum custos - forest warden at sumecica. three zubrinic households in one entry, each holding an office. this is a different social world from the blazevici , who are day labourers, or the papici , who carry sacks. nothing in the family tree records it. the godparent column is a second source for the offices read on 13 september 2026, for the first time. at the baptism of josephus zubrinic on 16 march 1845 the godparents are vitus kranjcevic, murarius - a mason - and maria zubrinic, mulier custodis carcerum, hujates : the wife of the prison keeper , of this place. that matters beyond the two names. the argument above rests on the parents' column and the 1834 entry; this is the same claim arriving from a different column of a different year , and it adds an office - custos carcerum - held in a zubrinic household. the latin otocac registers give every godparent a trade or a rank, and nobody had read that column until now . what has been searched → a note on the page itself the 1834 leaf is torn and has been conservation-mounted; the scan carries the archive's own label, repaired document / restaurirani
